title: Ruflo MCP bridge -- T1190 unauthenticated tools/call to terminal_execute
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-59726 (GHSA-c4hm-4h84-2cf3,
CVSS 10.0 CRITICAL), a self-reported advisory from Ruflo -- an agent
meta-harness for Claude Code and Codex.

Prior to 3.16.3, Ruflo's default `docker-compose` deployment bound the
MCP bridge to all network interfaces (not loopback-only) and exposed
`POST /mcp` and `POST /mcp/:group` without authentication. The advisory
states the tool blocklist that was supposed to cover `terminal_execute`
"was enforced only in the autopilot flow" -- these two HTTP endpoints
bypassed it entirely, so any unauthenticated network caller could invoke
`tools/call` against `terminal_execute`, obtain a shell in the bridge
container as the `node` user, read provider API keys from the container
environment, and poison the AgentDB learning-store with attacker-chosen
patterns.

Detection logic flags a JSON-RPC `tools/call` request whose `params.name`
is `terminal_execute`, arriving over HTTP without the bearer-token header
the fix later requires -- the MCP protocol's tool-invocation envelope is
the discriminator, not a generic "suspicious HTTP POST" heuristic. This is
the first rule in this corpus targeting the MCP protocol's own request
shape rather than a downstream OS-level effect, since this plugin is
itself an MCP server and the technique is directly relevant to its own
threat model.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (Ruflo, via GHSA
and NVD), fixed in 3.16.3.
